content.comment_body: I encountered an error message when trying to upload a project from [product_name] Web Editor to AWS. In [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no], uploading a test program works fine as a Device Shadow document. However, when creating a program in [product_name] Web Editor and attempting to upload it, I receive the attached error message. Can anyone advise what could be wrong and how to make it work as a web page for [product_name] Web Editor?

Hello [user_name], the screenshot you attached seems incorrect, but I experienced a similar error: "unable to update the environment with the new version of the [product_name] Web Editor application." I resolved it by manually creating a new environment, avoiding [product_name] Web Editor [version_no]. If the new environment works, try deploying your project there again and set up another new environment. Also, check out the suggested workarounds from [company_name]: one is to manually deploy the project to AWS. Note that the AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess permission is no longer available, which can cause issues. You may be missing some necessary AWS permissions for [product_name] Web Editor integration.
Can you clarify what you mean by 'create a new environment manually (without [product_name] Web Editor [version_no])'? How do I create this environment, is it done directly in AWS?

We've successfully operated a SCADA system for [product_name] [version_no] on AWS. I’ve shared a link to a YouTube video I made explaining the process. In a follow-up video, I’ll describe how to configure your AWS account. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience errors when uploading a project from [product_name] Web Editor to AWS, while uploads using [product_name] Soft Comfort for device shadow documents proceed without issues. Confusion exists around the deployment process and how to manually create environments in AWS for [product_name] Web Editor projects. The discussion mentions missing AWS permissions, such as AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess, and points out the lack of clear documentation and guidance for integrating [product_name] Web Editor with AWS. Community workarounds and external video tutorials are being relied upon due to insufficient in-app support for cloud deployment.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth uploads from [product_name] Web Editor to AWS, clear instructions on creating AWS environments, and adequate documentation or in-app guidance to help troubleshoot upload errors.
